description: Explains why salt, sugar and oil behave differently in water using solvation, molecular polarity, Gibbs energy, saturation, electrolytes and colligative effects.

related_resources.reason: Electrolytes, saturation, Henry law and osmotic effects.

historical_claims.anchor: Water molecules can then surround the separated ions
historical_claims.source_locator: Hydration, ion dipole orientation and energy accounting.

historical_claims.anchor: Sodium chloride dissolves readily even though its dissolution is slightly endothermic
historical_claims.source_locator: Dissolution heat, entropy and temperature-dependent solubility.

historical_claims.anchor: A solution that appears motionless still contains molecules and ions moving
historical_claims.source_locator: Dynamic solution equilibrium and molecular transport.

historical_claims.anchor: Henry's law describes an approximate relation
historical_claims.source_locator: Gas concentration proportional to partial pressure under appropriate dilute conditions.

authorship.scope: Original audio-first chemical science narration, examples, scientific companion, sources and metadata.
